phylogenetic_basis: Bohs et al. 2007 Acta Horticulturae 745 DOI 10.17660/ActaHortic.2007.745.8; Stern et al. 2010 Systematic Botany DOI 10.1600/036364410X539934
notes: Section Crinitum is sister to section Androceras and includes S. lycocarpum; Crinitum representatives are actinomorphic and isantherous. S. lycocarpum has primary floral-visitor evidence for bee pollination. S. lycocarpum is provisionally preferred over S. crinitum because equivalent close-section status is paired with stronger resolved pollination-source coverage. No BALANCE predictor value was used in selection.

phylogenetic_basis: Jiang et al. 2021 Journal of Systematics and Evolution DOI 10.1111/jse.12744; M. australasica is sister to the rest of Monochoria while M. korsakowii is the second split
notes: M. australasica is congeneric and explicitly lacks a morphologically distinct pollinating anther: six yellow anthers are arranged centrally. Comparative enantiostyly work treats enantiostylous taxa as animal-pollinated. It is not the sister species of M. korsakowii, so the match remains screened rather than adjudicated. No BALANCE predictor value was used in control selection.

phylogenetic_basis: Jiang_et_al_2021_JSE places M. australasica sister to the rest of Monochoria; M. vaginalis occurs in the derived remainder. Same control is shared with M. korsakowii and dependence must be retained.
notes: M. australasica has six yellow feeding anthers and no morphologically distinct pollinating anther in Jesson et al. 2003. Amegilla flower records document bee use. The control is not the sister species and is shared by two Monochoria cases, so no independent-replication claim is licensed.

phylogenetic_basis: Marazzi et al. 2006 place the all-10-fertile-stamen Psilorhegma condition within Senna; S. surattensis is a source-resolved congeneric contrast rather than a claimed sister species.
notes: Luo et al. 2009 directly compare S. alata and S. surattensis: S. alata has strongly differentiated stamen types whereas S. surattensis has all 10 stamens fertile and similar in size. Xylocopa are principal floral visitors and buzz all anthers in S. surattensis. Selected for direct same-study source comparability, not predictor contrast.

phylogenetic_basis: Marazzi et al. 2006 provide the Senna phylogenetic framework; S. surattensis is a congeneric source-matched contrast, not claimed to be the sister species of S. bicapsularis.
notes: Luo et al. 2009 directly compare S. bicapsularis and S. surattensis; the former has differentiated feeding/pollinating stamen sets while the latter lacks that differentiation. Xylocopa visit both. The same S. surattensis control is shared with S. alata, so shared-control dependence must be represented.

phylogenetic_basis: Chen et al. 2025 TAXON DOI 10.1002/tax.13349 recover Osbeckia chinensis plus O. nepalensis as the lineage sister to Melastoma; Flora of China describes Osbeckia stamens as isomorphic and equal or subequal.
notes: Selected before BALANCE predictor extraction. van der Pijl 1939 directly observed multiple hymenopterans visiting O. chinensis; bee-sized visitors landed on the stamen bundle and contacted the stigma with the abdomen, supporting animal-pollination eligibility. Flora of China independently records isomorphic equal/subequal stamens, excluding the feeding-versus-pollinating heteranthery used to define the case. Modern phylogenomics places the O. chinensis/O. nepalensis lineage sister to Melastoma. Match remains SCREENED because it is same-tribe/sister-lineage rather than congeneric and no claim of a species-level sister pair is made.
